title.zh: 卷373 列傳一百六十 宗室奕山 隆文 宗室奕经 文蔚 特依顺 余步雲
title.en: Volume 373 Biographies 160: Zong Shiyishan, Long Wen, Zong Shiyijing, Wen Wei, Te Yi Shun, Yu Buyun
title.raw: 卷373 列傳一百六十 宗室奕山 隆文 宗室奕经 文蔚 特依顺 余步雲

sentences.zh: =宗室奕山=宗室奕山，恂郡王允禵四世孫，隸鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: [Biography of] Imperial Clansman Yishan. Imperial Clansman Yishan was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun, Yinreng, and was registered in the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: [Biography of] Imperial Clansman Yishan. Yishan was a fourth-generation descendant of Prince Xun, Yinreng, and belonged to the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 授乾清門侍衛。

translations.literal: He was appointed attendant of the Gate of Heavenly Purity.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity.

sentences.zh: 道光七年，從征喀什噶爾，擢頭等侍衛、御前行走。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daoguang he followed the campaign against Kashgar and was promoted to first-class attendant with the privilege of walking before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Daoguang reign (1827), he took part in the campaign against Kashgar and was promoted to first-class attendant with the privilege of attending before the throne.

sentences.zh: 歷伊犁領隊大臣、參贊大臣。

translations.literal: He successively served as brigade commander at Ili and as assistant commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as brigade commander at Ili and as assistant commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授伊犁將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed military governor of Ili.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1838) he was appointed military governor of Ili.

sentences.zh: 二十年，偕副都統關福赴塔什圖畢治墾務，闢田十六萬四千馀畝，奏請置回千戶及五品伯克以下官。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, together with vice commander-in-chief Guan Fu, he went to Tashkent to oversee land reclamation, opened more than 164,000 mu of fields, and memorialized requesting the establishment of a thousand Hui households and officials from fifth-rank bokh down.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1840), he went with Vice Commander-in-Chief Guan Fu to Tashkent to oversee reclamation, opened more than 164,000 mu of farmland, and memorialized for the establishment of a thousand Hui households and officials from fifth-rank bokh downward.

sentences.zh: 召授正白旗領侍衛內大臣、御前大臣。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed leading attendant grandee of the Plain White Banner and grand minister in attendance before the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed leading attendant grandee of the Plain White Banner and a grand minister in attendance before the throne.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，命為靖逆將軍，督師廣東，尚書​​隆文、提督楊芳為參贊副之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to be Pacification General, to command the army in Guangdong, with Minister Long Wen and Provincial Military Commander Yang Fang as assistant commanders under him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1841) he was appointed Pacification General to command forces in Guangdong, with Minister Long Wen and Provincial Military Commander Yang Fang as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 時英兵已陷虎門，楊芳先至，聽美利堅人居間，乞許通商，被嚴斥，促奕山速赴軍。

translations.literal: At that time the English army had already taken Humen. Yang Fang arrived first, listened to Americans acting as intermediaries, and begged permission for trade; he was severely reprimanded, and Yishan was urged to hurry to the army.
translations.idiomatic: By then British forces had already captured Humen. Yang Fang arrived first, listened to American intermediaries, and petitioned to allow trade; he was sharply rebuked, and Yishan was ordered to hurry to the front.

sentences.zh: 三月，抵廣州。

translations.literal: In the third month he reached Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he reached Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 英艦橫亙省河，奕山問計於林則徐，則徐議先遣洋商設法羈縻，俾英艦暫退；

translations.literal: English warships stretched across the provincial river. Yishan sought counsel from Lin Zexu. Zexu proposed first sending foreign merchants to devise means of restraint so that the English ships might temporarily withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: British warships lay across the provincial river. Yishan asked Lin Zexu for advice. Lin proposed first having foreign merchants devise a way to restrain them so the British fleet might withdraw temporarily;

sentences.zh: 塞河道，積沙囊於岸以御砲，然後以守為攻。

translations.literal: block the river channel, pile sandbags on the banks to defend against cannon, and then take defense as attack.
translations.idiomatic: block the river channel, pile sandbags along the banks against cannon fire, and then turn defense into attack.

sentences.zh: 奕山不能用，且自琦善撤防，舊儲木椿鉅石皆為敵移去，時以杉板小船游弋以誘我師。

translations.literal: Yishan could not adopt this. Moreover, since Qishan had withdrawn the defenses, the old stores of wooden piles and great stones had all been removed by the enemy, who at the time used small fir-plank boats cruising about to lure our army.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan could not adopt the plan. Moreover, after Qishan had withdrawn the defenses, the old stores of wooden piles and great stones had all been removed by the enemy, who now sent small fir-plank boats cruising about to bait our forces.

sentences.zh: 楊芳主持重，以募勇未集，不欲浪戰。

translations.literal: Yang Fang held the chief responsibility and, because the recruited braves were not yet assembled, did not wish to fight recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fang held chief command and, because the recruited braves were not yet assembled, did not wish to fight recklessly.

sentences.zh: 奕山初亦然之，既而惑於左右言，欲僥倖一試，芳止之不可。

translations.literal: At first Yishan agreed with this, but then, misled by those around him, he wished to try his luck once; Fang could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yishan agreed, but then, swayed by those around him, he wished to gamble on one attempt; Fang could not dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 夜進兵，乘風毀七艘，報捷，詰旦乃知誤焚民舟，而英兵大至，連舟抵城下；

translations.literal: At night he advanced troops, and riding the wind destroyed seven vessels and reported victory; at dawn it was learned that civilian boats had been burned by mistake, while the English army came in force and linked their boats below the city;
translations.idiomatic: He advanced troops by night and, riding the wind, destroyed seven vessels and reported victory; at dawn it turned out that civilian boats had been burned by mistake, while the British army came in force and linked their ships below the city walls;

sentences.zh: 禦於河南，互有殺傷，遂閉城。

translations.literal: They defended at Henan with mutual casualties, and then closed the city.
translations.idiomatic: They fought at Henan with casualties on both sides, then shut the city gates.

sentences.zh: 敵以輪船襲泥城，副將岱昌等聞砲先遁，毀師船六十有奇，城外東西砲台並陷。

translations.literal: The enemy used steamships to attack Nicheng. Deputy generals Dai Chang and others fled at the sound of cannon; more than sixty government vessels were destroyed, and the eastern and western batteries outside the city all fell.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy attacked Nicheng with steamships. Deputy generals Dai Chang and others fled at the first cannon fire; more than sixty government vessels were destroyed, and the eastern and western batteries outside the city all fell.

sentences.zh: 英兵進踞後山四方砲台，奕山居貢院，砲火及焉，軍民惶懼，乃遣廣州知府餘保純出城見義律議息兵。

translations.literal: The English army advanced and seized the four batteries on Rear Hill. Yishan lodged in the examination compound, and cannon fire reached there; soldiers and civilians were terrified, so he sent Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun out of the city to see Elliot and discuss a ceasefire.
translations.idiomatic: British forces advanced and occupied the four batteries on Rear Hill. Yishan stayed in the examination compound, where cannon fire reached him; soldiers and civilians panicked, and he sent Guangzhou Prefect Yu Baochun out of the city to negotiate a ceasefire with Elliot.

sentences.zh: 義律索煙價千二百萬，美商居間減其半，並許給香港全島，英兵乃退。

translations.literal: Elliot demanded twelve million in opium indemnity; American merchants acting as intermediaries reduced it by half, and Hong Kong Island in its entirety was also granted; the English army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Elliot demanded twelve million taels in opium indemnity; American merchants acting as intermediaries cut the sum in half, and the whole of Hong Kong Island was also granted; the British army then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 奕山偕隆文先退，屯距城六十里小金山，諱敗為勝。

translations.literal: Yishan and Long Wen withdrew first and encamped at Little Golden Hill, sixty li from the city, concealing defeat as victory.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan and Long Wen withdrew first and encamped at Little Golden Hill, sixty li from the city, passing off defeat as victory.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「義律窮蹙乞撫，照舊通商，改償費為追交商欠，由粵海關及籓運兩庫給之。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Elliot, pressed to extremity, begged for appeasement; trade was to continue as before; compensation was changed to recovery of commercial debts owed, to be paid from the Guangdong Customs and the tribute-transport treasuries."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Elliot, driven to extremity, begged for appeasement; trade would continue as before; the indemnity was recast as recovery of commercial debts, to be paid from the Guangdong Customs and the tribute-transport treasuries."

sentences.zh: 」宣宗覽奏，以夷情恭順，詔允所請。

translations.literal: The Daoguang Emperor read the memorial and, believing the foreigners submissive, issued an edict approving the request.
translations.idiomatic: When the Daoguang Emperor read the memorial, believing the foreigners submissive, he issued an edict approving the request.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督顏伯燾迭疏劾其欺罔，下廣西巡撫梁章鉅察奏，乃得其狀，報聞。

translations.literal: Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang Yan Botao repeatedly memorialized impeaching him for deception; the case was referred to Guangxi Governor Liang Zhangju for investigation and report, and the true situation was obtained and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang Yan Botao repeatedly memorialized accusing him of deception; the matter was referred to Guangxi Governor Liang Zhangju for investigation, and the true facts were established and reported.

sentences.zh: 英人既得賂於粵，移兵犯閩、浙。

translations.literal: After the English had received their payment in Guangdong, they shifted troops to attack Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Once the British had received their payment in Guangdong, they moved their forces to attack Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 奕山等始收回大黃、獵德、虎門諸砲台，填塞省河。

translations.literal: Yishan and the others then recovered the batteries at Dahuang, Liede, Humen, and elsewhere, and filled in the provincial river.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan and his colleagues then recovered the batteries at Dahuang, Liede, Humen, and elsewhere, and blocked the provincial river.

sentences.zh: 鄉民於義律未退時，困之三元里，餘保純趨救始得出。

translations.literal: While Elliot had not yet withdrawn, the villagers trapped him at Sanyuanli; Yu Baochun rushed to rescue him before he could get out.
translations.idiomatic: While Elliot had not yet withdrawn, local militia trapped him at Sanyuanli; only when Yu Baochun rushed to rescue him could he escape.

sentences.zh: 於是團練日盛，中外皆言粵民可用，遂撤客軍，改募練勇。

translations.literal: Thereupon local militia training grew daily; at home and abroad all said the Guangdong people could be used, and outside troops were withdrawn and local militia recruited instead.
translations.idiomatic: Local militia training then flourished daily; at court and abroad all said the Guangdong people could be relied on, outside troops were withdrawn, and local militia were recruited instead.

sentences.zh: 迭詔趣奕山等規复香港，實不能戰，惟屢疏陳颶風漂沒敵船，毀香港蓬藔，藉修砲台未竣、造船未就為詞，以塞嚴詔。

translations.literal: Edicts repeatedly urged Yishan and the others to recover Hong Kong; in fact they could not fight, but only repeatedly memorialized that typhoons had sunk enemy ships and destroyed Hong Kong's thatched huts, using unfinished batteries and uncompleted shipbuilding as excuses to satisfy stern orders.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts repeatedly urged Yishan and the others to recover Hong Kong; they could not actually fight, but only repeatedly memorialized that typhoons had sunk enemy ships and destroyed Hong Kong's thatched shelters, citing unfinished batteries and uncompleted shipbuilding to satisfy stern orders.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，英人撤義律回國，以濮鼎查代之，大舉犯浙江、江蘇。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the English recalled Elliot to their country and replaced him with Pottinger, who launched a major attack on Zhejiang and Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1842) the British recalled Elliot and replaced him with Pottinger, who launched a major offensive against Zhejiang and Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 詔斥奕山陳奏欺詐，嚴議褫御前大臣、領侍衛內大臣、左都御史，仍留漢軍都統任。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Yishan for fraudulent memorials and ordered severe deliberation stripping him of grand minister before the throne, leading attendant grandee, and censor-in-chief, while retaining the post of commander-in-chief of the Han Banners.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked Yishan for fraudulent reports and ordered severe deliberation stripping him of grand minister before the throne, leading attendant grandee, and censor-in-chief, while retaining his post as commander-in-chief of the Han Banners.

sentences.zh: 及和議定，追論援粵失機，褫職治罪，論大辟，圈禁宗人府空室。

translations.literal: When the peace settlement was concluded, he was retrospectively judged for missing the opportunity when reinforcing Guangdong, stripped of office and punished, sentenced to death, and confined in an empty room of the Imperial Clansmen's Court.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was concluded, he was retrospectively condemned for missing the chance to save Guangdong, stripped of office and punished, sentenced to death, and confined in an empty room of the Imperial Clansmen's Court.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，釋之，予二等侍衛，充和闐辦事大臣，調伊犁參贊大臣，署將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was released, given second-class attendant, appointed commissioner at Khotan, transferred to assistant commissioner at Ili, and acted as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year (1843) he was released, given second-class attendant, appointed commissioner at Khotan, transferred to assistant commissioner at Ili, and served as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，調葉爾羌參贊大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year (1847) he was transferred to assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 安集延布魯特、回匪入邊，圍喀什噶爾、英吉沙爾，命陝甘總督布彥泰督師討之，奕山為副，連破賊於科科熱依瓦特及蘇噶特布拉克，賊遁走。

translations.literal: Kokand Bukharans and Hui rebels crossed the border, besieging Kashgar and Yengisar. Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Buyantai was ordered to command the army against them; Yishan served as his deputy and repeatedly defeated the rebels at Kokoryavat and Sugatbulak; the rebels fled.
translations.idiomatic: Kokand Bukharans and Hui rebels crossed the border and besieged Kashgar and Yengisar. Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Buyantai was ordered to command the punitive force; Yishan served as his deputy and repeatedly defeated the rebels at Kokoryavat and Sugatbulak, after which they fled.

sentences.zh: 論功，封二等鎮國將軍，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as second-rank Defender Prince of the State and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was enfeoffed as second-rank Defender Prince of the State and granted the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋授內閣學士，調伊犁參贊大臣，兼鑲黃旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed inner court academician, transferred to assistant commissioner at Ili, and concurrently made Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed inner court academician, transferred to assistant commissioner at Ili, and concurrently made Mongol commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授伊犁將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed military governor of Ili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1849) he was appointed military governor of Ili.

sentences.zh: 俄羅斯遣使至伊犁，請於伊犁、塔爾巴哈台、喀什噶爾三處通商，詔允其二，惟喀什噶爾不許。

translations.literal: Russia sent envoys to Ili requesting trade at Ili, Tarbagatai, and Kashgar in three places; an edict permitted two of them, but Kashgar was not allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Russia sent envoys to Ili requesting trade at Ili, Tarbagatai, and Kashgar; an edict permitted two of the three, but Kashgar was refused.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，俄人復固請，仍拒之，偕參贊布彥泰與定伊塔通商章程十七條。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng the Russians again pressed the request and were still refused; together with Assistant Commissioner Buyantai he fixed the seventeen articles of the Ili-Tarbagatai trade regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng (1851) the Russians again pressed the request and were still refused; together with Assistant Commissioner Buyantai he drew up the seventeen articles of the Ili-Tarbagatai trade regulations.

sentences.zh: 祭酒勝保疏論當仿恰克圖通商舊例，限以時日、人數。

translations.literal: Libationer Sheng Bao memorialized that the old precedent of trade at Kyakhta should be followed, limiting days and numbers of persons.
translations.idiomatic: Libationer Sheng Bao memorialized that the old Kyakhta trade precedent should be followed, limiting days and numbers of persons.

sentences.zh: 奕山議：「撫馭外夷以信為主，既已議定章程，旋改必有藉口。

translations.literal: Yishan argued: "In managing outer barbarians, good faith is primary; once regulations have been agreed upon, to change them at once would certainly give them a pretext."
translations.idiomatic: Yishan argued: "In managing foreign powers, good faith is paramount; once regulations have been agreed, to change them immediately would certainly give them a pretext."

sentences.zh: 」如所請行。

translations.literal: It was carried out as he requested.
translations.idiomatic: The court carried out his proposal.

sentences.zh: 累授內大臣、御前大臣，仍留將軍任。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed grand minister and grand minister before the throne while retaining the post of military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed grand minister and grand minister before the throne while retaining the post of military governor.

sentences.zh: 五年，調黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to military governor of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1855) he was transferred to military governor of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 時俄羅斯以分界為名，欲得黑龍江、松花江左岸地，遣艦入精奇里江，建屋於霍爾托庫、圖勒密、布雅里。

translations.literal: At that time Russia, under the name of boundary demarcation, wished to obtain the lands on the left banks of the Heilong and Songhua rivers, sent warships into the Zeya River, and built houses at Khortoku, Tulemi, and Buyari.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Russia, under the pretext of boundary demarcation, sought the lands on the left banks of the Amur and Sungari, sent warships into the Zeya River, and built houses at Khortoku, Tulemi, and Buyari.

sentences.zh: 奕山疏陳陽撫陰防之策。

translations.literal: Yishan memorialized stating a policy of open appeasement and covert defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan memorialized outlining a policy of open appeasement and covert defense.

sentences.zh: 七年，俄使請入京，拒不許。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Russian envoy requested entry to the capital and was refused permission.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (1857) the Russian envoy requested entry to the capital and was refused.

sentences.zh: 八年，俄人偕英、法、美三國合兵犯天津。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Russians joined England, France, and the United States in a combined attack on Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (1858) the Russians joined Britain, France, and the United States in a combined attack on Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 三國窺商利，而俄志在邊地，於是俄使木里裴岳幅至愛琿，堅請畫界，奕山允自額爾古納河口循黑龍江至松花江左岸之地盡屬之俄。

translations.literal: The three countries eyed commercial profit, while Russia's aim lay in borderlands; thereupon the Russian envoy Muravyov came to Aigun and pressed for boundary demarcation. Yishan agreed that all lands from the Argun mouth along the Heilong to the left bank of the Sungari should belong to Russia.
translations.idiomatic: The three Western powers sought commercial gain, while Russia aimed at territory; the Russian envoy Muravyov then came to Aigun and pressed for demarcation. Yishan agreed that all lands from the Argun mouth along the Amur to the left bank of the Sungari should belong to Russia.

sentences.zh: 俄使知奕山昧於地勢，駐兵黑龍江口，复索綏芬河、烏蘇里江地，奕山懾其兵威，勿能抗，疏稱未許，然已告俄使可比照海口等處辦理。

translations.literal: The Russian envoy, knowing Yishan was ignorant of geography, stationed troops at the mouth of the Heilong and again demanded the lands of the Suifen and Ussuri rivers. Yishan was cowed by their military might and could not resist; in his memorial he said he had not agreed, yet he had already told the Russian envoy it could be handled like the treaty ports.
translations.idiomatic: The Russian envoy, knowing Yishan was ignorant of the terrain, stationed troops at the mouth of the Amur and again demanded the Suifen and Ussuri regions. Yishan was cowed by their military power and could not resist; his memorial claimed he had not agreed, yet he had already told the Russian envoy it could be handled like the treaty ports.

sentences.zh: 逾年，與俄使會於愛琿，定約三條，鑱滿、蒙、漢三體字為界碑。

translations.literal: The following year he met the Russian envoy at Aigun and fixed three articles of treaty, carving boundary markers in Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he met the Russian envoy at Aigun and concluded a treaty of three articles, carving boundary markers in Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 大理寺少卿殷兆鏞劾奕山：「以邊地五千馀裡，藉稱閒曠，不候諭旨，拱手授人，始既輕諾，繼复受人所製，無能轉圜。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Yin Zhaoyong impeached Yishan: "For more than five thousand li of borderland, on the pretext that it was idle and vacant, without awaiting imperial instruction he handed it over with empty hands; at first he lightly promised, then again accepted what others imposed on him, and was unable to turn the situation around."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Yin Zhaoyong impeached Yishan: "For more than five thousand li of borderland, on the pretext that it was idle and vacant, without awaiting imperial instruction he surrendered it with empty hands; at first he promised lightly, then again accepted what others dictated, and was unable to recover the situation."

sentences.zh: 」詔切責之，革職留任；

translations.literal: An edict sharply rebuked him and stripped his office while retaining him in his post;
translations.idiomatic: An edict sharply rebuked him and stripped his office while retaining him in his post;

sentences.zh: 又以縱俄艦往黑龍江不之阻，褫御前大臣，召回京。

translations.literal: also because he had allowed Russian warships to go up the Heilong without blocking them, he was stripped of grand minister before the throne and recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: also because he had allowed Russian warships to ascend the Amur without blocking them, he was stripped of grand minister before the throne and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一年，聯軍在京定約，因奕山前議，自烏蘇里江口而南逾興凱湖，至綏芬河、瑚布圖河口，复沿琿春河達圖們江口，以東盡與俄人，語具邦交志。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the allied armies fixed the treaty in the capital, because of Yishan's earlier agreement, from the mouth of the Ussuri south across Lake Xingkai to the Suifen and Hunchun rivers, then along the Hunchun River to the mouth of the Tumen, all lands to the east were given to the Russians, as set forth in the record of foreign relations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year (1861), when the allied armies concluded the treaty at the capital, building on Yishan's earlier agreements, from the mouth of the Ussuri south across Lake Xingkai to the Suifen and Hunchun rivers, then along the Hunchun River to the mouth of the Tumen, all lands to the east were ceded to Russia, as set forth in the record of foreign relations.

sentences.zh: 尋复御前大臣，補正紅旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was restored as grand minister before the throne and appointed Mongol commander-in-chief of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was restored as grand minister before the throne and appointed Mongol commander-in-chief of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 同治中，封一等鎮國將軍，授內大臣。

translations.literal: In the Tongzhi period he was enfeoffed as first-rank Defender Prince of the State and appointed grand minister.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongzhi reign he was enfeoffed as first-rank Defender Prince of the State and appointed grand minister.

sentences.zh: 以疾罷。

translations.literal: He retired on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，卒，諡莊簡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he died; his posthumous title was Zhuangjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu (1878) he died; his posthumous title was Zhuangjian.

sentences.zh: 子載鷟，理籓院侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Zaizhuo was vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zaizhuo served as vice minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

sentences.zh: 載鷟子溥瀚，鑲黃旗蒙古副都統；

translations.literal: Zaizhuo's son Puhan was Mongol vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner;
translations.idiomatic: Zaizhuo's son Puhan was Mongol vice commander-in-chief of the Bordered Yellow Banner;

sentences.zh: 孫毓照，一等奉國將軍。

translations.literal: his grandson Yuzhao was a first-rank Supporter Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: and his grandson Yuzhao was a first-rank Supporter Prince of the State.

sentences.zh: =隆文=隆文，伊爾根覺羅氏，滿洲正紅旗人。

translations.literal: [Biography of] Long Wen. Long Wen was of the Irgen Gioro clan and a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: [Biography of] Long Wen. Long Wen was of the Irgen Gioro clan and a Manchu of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士，散館改刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and after leaving the academy was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing (1808) he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and after leaving the academy was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 坐事罷職，捐复，授翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for an offense, purchased reinstatement, and was appointed Hanlin expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for an offense, bought reinstatement, and was appointed Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached inner court academician.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to inner court academician.

sentences.zh: 道光中，充駐藏大臣。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang period he served as resident commissioner in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign he served as resident commissioner in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部、戶部侍郎，左都御史，刑部、兵部尚書，軍機大臣。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice minister of the Ministries of Personnel and Revenue, censor-in-chief, minister of Justice and War, and grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice minister of the Ministries of Personnel and Revenue, censor-in-chief, minister of Justice and War, and grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 屢奉使出讞獄。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly sent out on imperial commission to try capital cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly sent out on imperial commission to try capital cases.

sentences.zh: 偕奕山督師廣東，意不相合，甫至，病，憂憤而卒，諡端毅。

translations.literal: Together with Yishan he commanded the army in Guangdong; their views did not agree. He had only just arrived when he fell ill, died in grief and anger, and was given the posthumous title Duanyi.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Yishan in commanding forces in Guangdong, but their views did not agree. He had only just arrived when he fell ill and died in grief and anger; his posthumous title was Duanyi.

sentences.zh: =宗室奕經=宗室奕經，成親王永瑆孫，貝勒綿懿子，承繼循郡王允璋後，隸鑲紅旗。

translations.literal: [Biography of] Imperial Clansman Yijing. Imperial Clansman Yijing was grandson of Prince Cheng, Yongxing, son of Beile Mianyi, succeeded after Prince Xun, Yunzhang, and was registered in the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: [Biography of] Imperial Clansman Yijing. Yijing was grandson of Prince Cheng, Yongxing, son of Beile Mianyi; he succeeded the line of Prince Xun, Yunzhang, and belonged to the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 授乾清門侍衛，歷奉宸院卿、內閣學士，兼副都統、護軍統​​領。

translations.literal: He was appointed attendant of the Gate of Heavenly Purity and successively served as director of the Imperial Household Department, inner court academician, and concurrently vice commander-in-chief and colonel of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity and served in turn as director of the Imperial Household Department, inner court academician, and concurrently vice commander-in-chief and colonel of the guards.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，坐失察惇親王肩輿擅入神武中門，褫兼職，留內閣學士任。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang, for failure to supervise when Prince Dun's sedan chair entered the Central Gate of the Divine Martial Gate without authorization, his concurrent posts were stripped while he retained the post of inner court academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daoguang (1823), for failure to supervise when Prince Dun's sedan chair entered the Central Gate of the Divine Martial Gate without authorization, his concurrent posts were stripped while he retained the post of inner court academician.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to vice minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1825) he was transferred to vice minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十年，從征喀什噶爾回匪，事平回京，歷吏部、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed the campaign against the Hui rebels of Kashgar; when the affair was settled he returned to the capital and successively served as vice minister of the Ministries of Personnel and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (1830) he took part in the campaign against the Kashgar Hui rebels; when the affair was settled he returned to the capital and served in turn as vice minister of the Ministries of Personnel and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十四年，出為黑龍江將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he went out as military governor of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1834) he was posted as military governor of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，召授吏部尚書，兼步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was summoned and appointed minister of Personnel, concurrently metropolitan garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year (1836) he was recalled and appointed minister of Personnel, concurrently metropolitan garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was made associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1841) he was made associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 英兵犯浙江，定海、鎮海及寧波府城相繼陷，裕謙死事，命為揚威將軍，督師往剿，都統哈哴阿、提督胡超為參贊，尋易侍郎文蔚、都統特依順副之。

translations.literal: When the English army attacked Zhejiang, Dinghai, Zhenhai, and the prefectural city of Ningbo fell in succession; Yu Qian died in service. Yijing was appointed Expelling-Awe General to command the army for suppression; Commander-in-Chief Halia and Provincial Military Commander Hu Chao served as assistants; soon Minister Wen Wei and Commander-in-Chief Te Yishun were substituted as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: When British forces attacked Zhejiang, Dinghai, Zhenhai, and the prefectural seat of Ningbo fell in succession; Yu Qian died in the field. Yijing was appointed Expelling-Awe General to command the punitive force; Commander-in-Chief Halia and Provincial Military Commander Hu Chao served as deputies; soon Minister Wen Wei and Commander-in-Chief Te Yishun replaced them.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，宣宗禦勤政殿，訓示方略，特詔：「申明軍紀，凡失守各城逃將逃兵，軍法從事。

translations.literal: On the day of his audience for departure, the Daoguang Emperor received him in the Hall of Diligent Government and instructed him in strategy; a special edict stated: "Make clear military discipline: all generals and soldiers who abandon cities they have lost shall be dealt with by military law."
translations.idiomatic: On the day he took leave, the Daoguang Emperor received him in the Hall of Diligent Government and instructed him in strategy; a special edict declared: "Make military discipline explicit: every general and soldier who abandons a lost city shall be dealt with by military law."

sentences.zh: 」發交內庫花翎等件，有功者立予懋賞，勉以恩威並用，整飭戎行。

translations.literal: He was given peacock feathers and other items from the inner treasury; those with merit were to receive generous rewards at once, and he was exhorted to use both kindness and severity and to put the army in order.
translations.idiomatic: He was given peacock feathers and other items from the inner treasury; the worthy were to receive generous rewards at once, and he was exhorted to combine kindness and severity and put the army in order.

sentences.zh: 大學士穆彰阿奏請釋琦善出獄，隨赴軍前效力，奕經卻之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Mujangga memorialized requesting the release of Qishan from prison to follow the army and serve; Yijing refused.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Mujangga memorialized to release Qishan from prison so he could serve at the front; Yijing refused.

sentences.zh: 奕經分屬懿親，素謹厚，為上所倚重，奉命專徵，頗欲有為而不更事，尤昧兵略。

translations.literal: Yijing belonged to the imperial clan and was by nature cautious and honest; the emperor relied on him heavily. Ordered on a special campaign, he wished to accomplish something but lacked experience, and was especially ignorant of military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: As an imperial clansman Yijing was by nature cautious and honest and was heavily relied on by the emperor. Ordered on an independent campaign, he wished to accomplish something but lacked experience and was especially ignorant of military strategy.

sentences.zh: 奏調陝甘、川、黔兵一萬人，請撥部餉一萬兩，倉猝未集，駐蘇州以待。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting ten thousand troops from Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan, and Guizhou and ten thousand taels from the ministry treasury; they could not be assembled in haste, and he encamped at Suzhou to wait.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for ten thousand troops from Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan, and Guizhou and ten thousand taels from the ministry treasury; neither could be assembled in haste, and he encamped at Suzhou to wait.

sentences.zh: 上以諸將少可恃者，命凡文武員弁及士民商賈有奇材異能一藝可取者，許詣軍前投效。

translations.literal: Because the emperor thought few of the generals could be relied on, he ordered that any civil or military official and any scholar, merchant, or person with a special talent or skill worth taking might present himself before the army.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor thought few generals could be trusted, he ordered that any civil or military official and any scholar, merchant, or person with unusual talent or a useful skill might present himself at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 奕經渡江後，於營門設木匭，納名即延見，且許密陳得失。

translations.literal: After Yijing crossed the river, he set up a wooden box at the camp gate; whoever submitted his name was received at once, and confidential statements of gain and loss were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Yijing crossed the Yangzi, he set up a wooden box at the camp gate; whoever submitted his name was received at once, and confidential advice on strengths and weaknesses was welcomed.

sentences.zh: 於是獻策者四百馀人，投效者一百四十馀人，而軍中所闢僚佐，多闒冗京員，投效者亦無異才。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than four hundred persons offered plans and more than one hundred forty presented themselves for service, but the staff officers appointed in the army were mostly idle Beijing officials, and those who presented themselves also had no unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred persons then offered plans and more than one hundred forty presented themselves for service, but the staff officers appointed in the army were mostly idle Beijing officials, and those who volunteered likewise had no unusual talent.

sentences.zh: 惟宿遷舉人臧紆青自負氣節，為言議撫徒損國威，始決主戰；

translations.literal: Only the Suqian licentiate Zang Yuqing, confident in his integrity, argued that to discuss appeasement would only harm national prestige, and only then was the decision made to fight;
translations.idiomatic: Only the Suqian licentiate Zang Yuqing, confident in his integrity, argued that talk of appeasement would only harm national prestige, and only then was the decision made to fight;

sentences.zh: 又勸劾斬失律提督余步雲以立威望，疏具而旋寢。

translations.literal: he also urged impeachment and execution of the delinquent Provincial Military Commander Yu Buyun to establish authority, but after the memorial was drafted it was soon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: he also urged impeachment and execution of the delinquent Provincial Military Commander Yu Buyun to establish authority, but after the memorial was drafted it was soon shelved.

sentences.zh: 以浙兵屢潰，不堪臨陣，召募山東、河南、安徽義勇。

translations.literal: Because the Zhejiang troops had repeatedly collapsed and could not face battle, he recruited volunteers from Shandong, Henan, and Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhejiang troops had repeatedly collapsed and could not face battle, he recruited volunteers from Shandong, Henan, and Anhui.

sentences.zh: 浙事日亟，巡撫劉韻珂促援，遲不至，遂相惡。

translations.literal: As affairs in Zhejiang grew daily more urgent, Governor Liu Yunke urged relief, but help was slow in coming; the two therefore came to dislike each other.
translations.idiomatic: As the Zhejiang crisis grew daily more urgent, Governor Liu Yunke urged relief, but help was slow in coming; the two therefore grew hostile.

sentences.zh: 久駐江蘇，以供應之累，官吏亦厭之，餉需文報，皆延擱不時應。

translations.literal: He remained long in Jiangsu; officials were also wearied by the burden of supplying him, and funds, supplies, and documents were all delayed and not answered in time.
translations.idiomatic: He remained long in Jiangsu; officials were wearied by the burden of supplying him, and funds, supplies, and documents were all delayed and answered late.

sentences.zh: 十二月，始抵杭州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he finally reached Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he finally reached Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 前泗州知州張應云獻策規复寧波，奕經、文蔚皆然之，遂令總理前敵營務。

translations.literal: Former Sizhou Prefect Zhang Yingyun offered a plan to recover Ningbo; Yijing and Wen Wei both approved it, and he was ordered to take general charge of front-line camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Former Sizhou Prefect Zhang Yingyun offered a plan to recover Ningbo; Yijing and Wen Wei both approved it, and he was ordered to take general charge of front-line camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 應云以重貲購寧波府吏陸心蘭為內應，日報機密多虛誑。

translations.literal: Yingyun used a heavy bribe to buy Ningbo prefectural clerk Lu Xinlan as an inside agent; his daily reports of secrets were mostly false.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyun used a heavy bribe to buy Ningbo prefectural clerk Lu Xinlan as an inside agent; his daily intelligence reports were mostly false.

sentences.zh: 奕經禱於西湖關廟，占得「虎頭」之兆，乃議於二十二年正月寅日寅時進兵，屢遣諜，為敵所獲，漏師期。

translations.literal: Yijing prayed at the Guandi Temple by West Lake and obtained the omen "tiger's head"; he then planned to advance troops on the yin day and yin hour of the first month of the twenty-second year, but spies he repeatedly sent were captured by the enemy and the date of the campaign leaked.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing prayed at the Guandi Temple by West Lake and obtained the omen "tiger's head"; he then planned to advance on the yin day and yin hour of the first month of the twenty-second year (1842), but spies he repeatedly sent were captured and the campaign date leaked.

sentences.zh: 初，英兵踞府城僅二三百人，艦泊定海。

translations.literal: At first the English army occupied the prefectural city with only two or three hundred men, and their ships lay at Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: At first the British held the prefectural city with only two or three hundred men, and their ships lay at Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 至是，濮鼎查率十九艘兵二千散泊江岸，早為之備矣。

translations.literal: By then Pottinger led nineteen vessels and two thousand troops scattered along the riverbanks, and preparations had long been made.
translations.idiomatic: By then Pottinger had led nineteen vessels and two thousand troops scattered along the riverbanks, and preparations were already complete.

sentences.zh: 奕經由紹興進曹娥江，而慈谿敵兵退。

translations.literal: Yijing advanced from Shaoxing into the Cao'e River, while the enemy at Cixi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing advanced from Shaoxing into the Cao'e River, while the enemy at Cixi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 應云請急進，遂駐慈谿東關，文蔚分屯長谿嶺，令提督段永福、余步雲等趨寧波，游擊劉天保趨鎮海，副將硃貴駐大寶山，而應云率所募義勇駐駱駝橋，為諸軍策應，約於正月晦數路並舉。

translations.literal: Yingyun urged a rapid advance; they then encamped at the East Pass of Cixi. Wen Wei divided forces at Changxi Ridge, ordered Provincial Military Commander Duan Yongfu, Yu Buyun, and others to hurry toward Ningbo, Ranger Liu Tianbao toward Zhenhai, and Deputy General Zhu Gui to hold Dabaoshan, while Yingyun led the volunteers he had recruited at Luotuo Bridge as support for the armies, agreeing to launch on the last day of the first month on several routes at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yingyun urged a rapid advance; they encamped at the East Pass of Cixi while Wen Wei divided forces at Changxi Ridge. He ordered Provincial Military Commander Duan Yongfu, Yu Buyun, and others toward Ningbo, Ranger Liu Tianbao toward Zhenhai, and Deputy General Zhu Gui to hold Dabaoshan, while Yingyun led his recruited volunteers at Luotuo Bridge to coordinate the armies, planning a simultaneous advance on the last day of the first month.

sentences.zh: 而敵已勾結應云部勇，勢且生變，不及待期，先二日輕軍分襲，不攜槍砲。

translations.literal: But the enemy had already won over Yingyun's volunteers; a mutiny was imminent, and they could not wait for the appointed day. Two days early they sent light detachments in separate raids without carrying muskets or cannon.
translations.idiomatic: But the enemy had already suborned Yingyun's volunteers; a mutiny was imminent, and they could not wait for the appointed day. Two days early they sent light detachments in separate raids without muskets or cannon.

sentences.zh: 永福等入寧波南門，中地雷，天保甫及鎮海城下，為敵砲擊退，皆大敗。

translations.literal: Yongfu and the others entered Ningbo's south gate and struck land mines. Tianbao had only just reached below Zhenhai city when he was beaten back by enemy cannon; all suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yongfu and the others entered Ningbo's south gate and struck land mines. Tianbao had only just reached Zhenhai when enemy cannon drove him back; all were routed.

sentences.zh: 越日，應云所具火攻船為敵所焚，軍中自驚，奔大寶山。

translations.literal: The next day the fire-attack boats Yingyun had prepared were burned by the enemy; the army panicked on its own and fled to Dabaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the fire ships Yingyun had prepared were burned by the enemy; the army panicked and fled to Dabaoshan.

sentences.zh: 硃貴收集潰兵圖進攻，敵兵已至，力戰竟日，殺傷相當，無援，貴死之。

translations.literal: Zhu Gui gathered the routed troops intending to attack; the enemy had already arrived. He fought fiercely all day with comparable casualties, but without reinforcements Gui died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui gathered the routed troops to counterattack, but the enemy was already there. He fought fiercely all day with comparable casualties; without reinforcements he was killed.

sentences.zh: 文蔚聞敗亦退，軍資器械棄失殆盡。

translations.literal: When Wen Wei heard of the defeat he also withdrew; military stores and weapons were abandoned almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Wei heard of the defeat he also withdrew; military stores and weapons were abandoned almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 奕經留軍紹興，回駐杭州，自請嚴議，詔原之。

translations.literal: Yijing left troops at Shaoxing and returned to encamp at Hangzhou, requesting severe deliberation on himself; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing left troops at Shaoxing and returned to Hangzhou, asking that he be severely punished; an edict pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 英艦乘勝由海窺錢塘江，以尖山海口淺阻，尋退去。

translations.literal: English ships, riding their victory, spied on the Qiantang River by sea, but because Jianshan harbor was shallow and obstructed they soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: British ships, riding their victory, probed the Qiantang River by sea, but Jianshan harbor was too shallow and obstructed, and they soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 鄭鼎臣者，殉難總兵國鴻子，曾從父軍。

translations.literal: Zheng Dingchen was son of the martyred regional commander Guo Hong and had once followed his father in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dingchen was the son of the martyred regional commander Guo Hong and had once served under his father.

sentences.zh: 奕經予二十四萬金，令募水勇規复定海，聞寧鎮之敗，逡巡海上。

translations.literal: Yijing gave him 240,000 taels and ordered him to recruit naval braves to recover Dinghai; when he heard of the defeats at Ningbo and Zhenhai he lingered at sea.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing gave him 240,000 taels and ordered him to recruit naval forces to recover Dinghai; when he heard of the defeats at Ningbo and Zhenhai he lingered at sea.

sentences.zh: 奕經督之嚴，乃報三月三日敗敵於定海十六門洋面，毀船數十，殲斃數百。

translations.literal: When Yijing pressed him severely, he then reported that on the third day of the third month he had defeated the enemy on the open sea at Dinghai's Sixteen Gates, destroyed several tens of ships, and killed several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When Yijing pressed him hard, he reported that on the third day of the third month he had defeated the enemy off Dinghai's Sixteen Gates, destroyed dozens of ships, and killed several hundred.

sentences.zh: 劉韻珂以為欺罔，奕經遣侍衛容照等出洋查勘，得焚毀船木及壞械回報，乃疏聞，賜奕經雙眼花翎，鼎臣亦被獎。

translations.literal: Liu Yunke regarded this as deception. Yijing sent Bodyguard Rong Zhao and others out to sea to investigate; they returned with burned ship timber and broken weapons as evidence, whereupon he memorialized and reported. Yijing was granted the double-eyed peacock feather and Dingchen was also rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yunke regarded this as fraud. Yijing sent Bodyguard Rong Zhao and others to investigate at sea; they returned with burned ship timber and broken weapons, whereupon he memorialized the victory. Yijing was granted the double-eyed peacock feather and Dingchen was also rewarded.

sentences.zh: 時寧波英兵忽退，留艦招寶山海口，改犯乍浦，陷之。

translations.literal: At that time the English troops at Ningbo suddenly withdrew, leaving ships at the mouth of Zhaobaoshan harbor, and shifted to attack Zhapu, which fell.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the British at Ningbo suddenly withdrew, leaving ships at Zhaobaoshan harbor, and shifted to attack Zhapu, which fell.

sentences.zh: 奕經不能赴援，而以收復寧波奏，詔斥不先事預防，革職留任。

translations.literal: Yijing could not go to the relief, yet memorialized the recovery of Ningbo; an edict rebuked him for failing to take preventive measures beforehand and stripped his office while retaining him in his post.
translations.idiomatic: Yijing could not go to the relief, yet memorialized the recovery of Ningbo; an edict rebuked him for failing to take preventive measures and stripped his office while retaining him in his post.

sentences.zh: 既而英兵犯江南，陷鎮江，逼江寧，命奕經赴援，尋命駐王江涇防禦。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the English army attacked Jiangnan, took Zhenjiang, and pressed Jiangning; Yijing was ordered to go to the relief, and soon afterward was ordered to encamp at Wangjiangjing for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward British forces attacked Jiangnan, took Zhenjiang, and pressed Jiangning; Yijing was ordered to reinforce, and soon was ordered to encamp at Wangjiangjing on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 奕經自寧波、慈谿之敗，軍心渙散，不能復用，益為劉韻珂所揶揄，議守議撫，一不使聞。

translations.literal: After the defeats at Ningbo and Cixi, Yijing's army morale collapsed and he could not be used again; he was further mocked by Liu Yunke, and discussions of defense and appeasement were kept from him entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeats at Ningbo and Cixi, army morale under Yijing collapsed and he could not be used again; Liu Yunke mocked him further, and discussions of defense and appeasement were kept from him entirely.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，撤師，詔布奕經等勞師糜餉、誤國殃民罪狀，逮京論大辟。

translations.literal: When the peace settlement was concluded the army was withdrawn; an edict published the crimes of Yijing and others for exhausting the army and wasting supplies and harming the state and the people, and they were arrested and brought to the capital for sentencing to death.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was concluded the army was withdrawn; an edict published the crimes of Yijing and others for exhausting troops, wasting supplies, and harming the state and people, and they were arrested and brought to the capital for sentencing to death.

sentences.zh: 圈禁逾年，與琦善同起用，予四等侍衛，充葉爾羌幫辦大臣。

translations.literal: After more than a year in confinement he was reemployed together with Qishan, given fourth-class attendant, and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in confinement he was reemployed together with Qishan, given fourth-class attendant, and appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 為御史陳慶鏞論劾，仍褫職。

translations.literal: Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized impeaching him, and he was again stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Chen Qingyong impeached him, and he was again stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复予二等侍衛，充葉爾羌參贊大臣，調伊犁領隊大臣。

translations.literal: Before long he was again given second-class attendant, appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand, and transferred to brigade commander at Ili.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again given second-class attendant, appointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand, and transferred to brigade commander at Ili.

sentences.zh: 坐審鞫英吉沙爾領隊大臣齋清額誣捕良回獄不當，褫職發黑龍江。

translations.literal: For trying the case of Yengisar Brigade Commander Zhai Qing'e, who had falsely arrested innocent Hui and imprisoned them improperly, he was stripped of office and sent to Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: For mishandling the trial of Yengisar Brigade Commander Zhai Qing'e, who had falsely arrested innocent Hui and imprisoned them improperly, he was stripped of office and sent to Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 三十年，釋回。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year (1850) he was released and returned.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，歷伊犁、英吉沙爾領隊大臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he successively served as brigade commander at Ili and Yengisar.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he served in turn as brigade commander at Ili and Yengisar.

sentences.zh: 二年，召授工部侍郎，調刑部，兼副都統。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned and appointed vice minister of Works, transferred to Punishments, and concurrently made vice commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (1852) he was summoned and appointed vice minister of Works, transferred to Punishments, and concurrently made vice commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三年，命率密雲駐防赴山東防粵匪，卒於徐州軍次，依侍郎例賜卹。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered to lead the Miyun garrison to Shandong against the Guangdong bandits and died on campaign at Xuzhou; he was granted funeral rites according to the precedent for vice ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (1853) he was ordered to lead the Miyun garrison to Shandong against the Taiping rebels and died on campaign at Xuzhou; he received funeral rites according to the precedent for vice ministers.

sentences.zh: =文蔚=文蔚，費莫氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: [Biography of] Wen Wei. Wen Wei was of the Feimo clan and a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: [Biography of] Wen Wei. Wen Wei was of the Feimo clan and a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二年進士，授翰林院檢討。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiaqing he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed Hanlin reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiaqing (1797) he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 累擢至兵部、工部侍郎，兼副都統、內務府大臣。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached vice minister of the Ministries of War and Works, concurrently vice commander-in-chief and minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to vice minister of the Ministries of War and Works, concurrently vice commander-in-chief and minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 方其駐長谿嶺也，聞諸路軍皆不利，欲移營走。

translations.literal: When he was encamped at Changxi Ridge, hearing that every route's army had met with ill fortune, he wished to move camp and flee.
translations.idiomatic: While he was encamped at Changxi Ridge, hearing that every column had met defeat, he wished to move camp and flee.

sentences.zh: 敵雜難民潰兵猝至，焚毀營帳，乃奔曹娥江，收集潰兵，退保紹興。

translations.literal: The enemy mixed with refugees and routed soldiers arrived suddenly, burned the camp tents, and he fled to the Cao'e River, gathered the routed troops, and withdrew to defend Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy mixed with refugees and routed troops arrived suddenly, burned the camp tents, and he fled to the Cao'e River, gathered the routed forces, and withdrew to defend Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 欲渡錢塘江，為劉韻珂所阻。

translations.literal: He wished to cross the Qiantang River but was blocked by Liu Yunke.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to cross the Qiantang River but was blocked by Liu Yunke.

sentences.zh: 尋以定海報捷，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because of the reported victory at Dinghai, he was given the first-class rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, because of the reported victory at Dinghai, he was given the first-class rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 軍事竣，追論失機，褫職下獄。

translations.literal: When military affairs were concluded he was retrospectively judged for missing the opportunity, stripped of office, and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When military affairs concluded he was retrospectively condemned for missing the opportunity, stripped of office, and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 逾年，釋出，予三等侍衛，充古城領隊大臣，复褫職。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was released, given third-class attendant, appointed brigade commander at Gucheng, and again stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was released, given third-class attendant, appointed brigade commander at Gucheng, and again stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，歷喀喇沙爾、哈密辦事大臣，駐藏大臣，奉天府尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he successively served as commissioner at Karashahr and Hami, resident commissioner in Tibet, and prefect of Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he served in turn as commissioner at Karashahr and Hami, resident commissioner in Tibet, and prefect of Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (1855) he died.

sentences.zh: =特依順=特依順，他塔喇氏，滿洲正藍旗人，福州駐防。

translations.literal: [Biography of] Te Yishun. Te Yishun was of the Tatara clan, a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner, and garrisoned at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: [Biography of] Te Yishun. Te Yishun was of the Tatara clan, a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner garrisoned at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷協領。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached assistant colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to assistant colonel.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，從平台灣張丙亂，擢荊州副都統。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he followed the suppression of Zhang Bing's rebellion in Pingtaiwan and was promoted to vice commander-in-chief of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang (1833) he took part in suppressing Zhang Bing's rebellion in Pingtaiwan and was promoted to vice commander-in-chief of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷騰越鎮總兵、密雲副都統、寧夏將軍。

translations.literal: He successively served as regional commander at Tengyue, vice commander-in-chief at Miyun, and military governor of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as regional commander at Tengyue, vice commander-in-chief at Miyun, and military governor of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，予都統銜，授參贊大臣，督師廣東。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was given commander-in-chief's rank, appointed assistant commander, and ordered to command the army in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1841) he was given commander-in-chief's rank, appointed assistant commander, and ordered to command forces in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋命改赴浙江辦理軍務，駐守省城，署杭州將軍，遂實授。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was ordered instead to go to Zhejiang to handle military affairs, garrison the provincial capital, act as military governor of Hangzhou, and then was appointed in full.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered instead to handle military affairs in Zhejiang, garrison the provincial capital, serve as acting military governor of Hangzhou, and then received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 乍浦陷，坐革職留任。

translations.literal: When Zhapu fell he was punished by stripping office while retaining him in his post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhapu fell he was stripped of office while retained in his post.

sentences.zh: 和議成，命籌辦浙江善後事宜。

translations.literal: When the peace settlement was concluded he was ordered to arrange Zhejiang's postwar affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was concluded he was ordered to arrange Zhejiang's postwar affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，調烏里雅蘇台將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was transferred to military governor of Uliastai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year (1846) he was transferred to military governor of Uliastai.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year (1849) he died.

sentences.zh: =余步雲=余步雲，四川廣安人。

translations.literal: [Biography of] Yu Buyun. Yu Buyun was a native of Guang'an in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: [Biography of] Yu Buyun. Yu Buyun was a native of Guang'an in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，以鄉勇從剿教匪，積功至游擊。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing period, as a village militiaman he followed campaigns against the sect rebels and through accumulated merit reached the rank of ranger.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiaqing reign, as a village militiaman he joined campaigns against the sect rebels and through accumulated merit rose to ranger.

sentences.zh: 平瞻對叛番，累擢重慶鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He pacified the rebellious Tibetans of Zhanzhdu and through successive promotions became regional commander of Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the rebellious Tibetans of Zhanzhdu and through successive promotions became regional commander of Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 道光七年，率本鎮兵從楊遇春徵回疆，破賊洋阿爾巴特莊；

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daoguang he led troops of his command in following Yang Yuchun's campaign in the Western Regions and defeated the rebels at Yang'a'erbat Village;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daoguang (1827) he led his command in Yang Yuchun's Western Regions campaign and defeated the rebels at Yang'a'erbat Village;

sentences.zh: 偕楊芳擊賊於毗拉滿，大敗之，復和闐，追擒賊酋玉努斯，授乾清門侍衛，擢貴州提督。

translations.literal: together with Yang Fang he attacked the rebels at Pilaman, inflicted a great defeat, recovered Khotan, pursued and captured the rebel chief Yunusi, was appointed attendant of the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and was promoted to provincial military commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: together with Yang Fang he attacked the rebels at Pilaman, routed them, recovered Khotan, pursued and captured the rebel chief Yunusi, was appointed attendant at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, and was promoted to provincial military commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 調湖南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，率貴州兵剿江華瑤趙金龍，偕提督羅思舉破賊巢，金龍就殲，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he led Guizhou troops to suppress the Yao Zhao Jinlong of Jianghua; together with Provincial Military Commander Luo Siju he destroyed the rebel nest and Jinlong was killed; he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year (1832) he led Guizhou troops against the Yao leader Zhao Jinlong of Jianghua; with Provincial Military Commander Luo Siju he destroyed the rebel stronghold and killed Jinlong; he received the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 复破粵瑤於永州藍山，擒其渠。

translations.literal: He again defeated the Guangdong Yao at Lanshan in Yongzhou and captured their leader.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Guangdong Yao at Lanshan in Yongzhou and captured their leader.

sentences.zh: 從尚書禧恩赴廣東剿連州瑤，平之，賜雙眼花翎，予一等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: He followed Minister Xi'en to Guangdong to suppress the Yao of Lianzhou, pacified them, was granted the double-eyed peacock feather, and was given the hereditary rank of first-class Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Minister Xi'en to Guangdong to suppress the Lianzhou Yao, pacified them, was granted the double-eyed peacock feather, and received the hereditary rank of first-class Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 歷四川、雲南提督，復調貴州。

translations.literal: He successively served as provincial military commander of Sichuan and Yunnan and was again transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as provincial military commander of Sichuan and Yunnan and was again transferred to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擒仁懷匪首謝法真，加太子太保，調福建提督。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he captured the bandit chief Xie Fazhen of Renhuai, was given the title Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and was transferred to provincial military commander of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year (1838) he captured the bandit chief Xie Fazhen of Renhuai, received the title Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and was transferred to provincial military commander of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 二十年，英兵初陷定海，率師赴援，調浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when the English army first took Dinghai, he led troops to the relief and was transferred to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year (1840), when British forces first took Dinghai, he led troops to the relief and was transferred to provincial military commander of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，定海既收還，步雲駐防鎮海。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, after Dinghai had been recovered, Buyun garrisoned Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year (1841), after Dinghai had been recovered, Buyun garrisoned Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 裕謙來督師，疏言步云不可恃，未及易而英兵猝至，复陷定海，三鎮戰歿。

translations.literal: When Yu Qian came to command the army he memorialized that Buyun could not be relied on; before he could be replaced the English army arrived suddenly, Dinghai again fell, and the three regional commanders died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Qian came to command the army he memorialized that Buyun could not be trusted; before he could be replaced the British arrived suddenly, Dinghai fell again, and the three regional commanders died in battle.

sentences.zh: 步雲屯招寶山，總兵謝朝恩分守金雞嶺。

translations.literal: Buyun encamped at Zhaobaoshan; Regional Commander Xie Chao'en separately defended Jinjiling.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun encamped at Zhaobaoshan while Regional Commander Xie Chao'en separately defended Jinjiling.

sentences.zh: 步雲號宿將，實巧猾無戰志，又嗛裕謙剛愎，將戰，裕謙召與盟神誓師，託疾不赴，且獻緩敵之策。

translations.literal: Buyun was styled a veteran general but was in fact crafty and slippery and without fighting will; he also resented Yu Qian's stubbornness. When battle was imminent Yu Qian summoned him to swear an oath before the gods and review the army, but he pleaded illness and did not go, and moreover offered a plan to slow the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun was styled a veteran general but was in fact crafty and cowardly; he also resented Yu Qian's stubbornness. When battle was imminent Yu Qian summoned him to swear an oath and review the troops, but he pleaded illness and stayed away, offering instead a plan to delay the enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵攻其前，而以小舟載兵由石洞攀援登後山，步雲遽棄砲台走，敵乃據招寶山俯擊鎮海城，金雞嶺及縣城先後陷。

translations.literal: The enemy attacked in front while small boats carried troops up through stone caves to climb Rear Hill by rope; Buyun abruptly abandoned the battery and fled. The enemy then seized Zhaobaoshan and fired down on Zhenhai city; Jinjiling and the county seat fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy attacked in front while small boats carried troops through stone caves to climb Rear Hill; Buyun abruptly abandoned the battery and fled. The enemy seized Zhaobaoshan and fired down on Zhenhai; Jinjiling and the county seat fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 步雲退寧波，敵掩至，墜馬傷足，僅免，府城遂陷。

translations.literal: Buyun retreated to Ningbo; the enemy came upon him suddenly; he fell from his horse and injured his foot, barely escaping, and the prefectural city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun retreated to Ningbo; the enemy overtook him; he fell from his horse and injured his foot, barely escaping, and the prefectural city then fell.

sentences.zh: 步雲疏聞，委敗於裕謙。

translations.literal: In his memorial Buyun attributed the defeat to Yu Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial Buyun blamed the defeat on Yu Qian.

sentences.zh: 裕謙既歿，其妻赴京訟之。

translations.literal: After Yu Qian had died, his wife went to the capital to sue Buyun.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu Qian died, his wife went to the capital to prosecute Buyun.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，從奕經規复寧波，不克，褫步雲職，逮京，命軍機大臣會刑部訊鞫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he followed Yijing in the plan to recover Ningbo but did not succeed; Buyun was stripped of office, arrested, and brought to the capital; the grand councilors were ordered to join the Ministry of Punishments in trying him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year (1842) he followed Yijing's plan to recover Ningbo but failed; Buyun was stripped of office, arrested, and brought to the capital for trial by the grand councilors and the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 廷臣爭劾其罪，亦有原之者，獄久延，尚書李振祜堅持，讞乃定。

translations.literal: Court officials competed in impeaching his crimes, though some also pleaded for him; the case dragged on for a long time until Minister Li Zhenhu held firm and the verdict was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials competed in impeaching him, though some pleaded for mercy; the case dragged on until Minister Li Zhenhu held firm and the verdict was fixed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「餘步雲膺海疆重寄，未陣獲一賊，身受一傷，首先退縮，以致將士效尤，奔潰棄城，直同兒戲。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Yu Buyun bore the heavy trust of the maritime frontier, yet in battle captured not a single enemy, received but one wound, and was the first to shrink back, causing officers and soldiers to follow his example, rout the army, and abandon cities — the whole affair was child's play."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "Yu Buyun bore the heavy trust of the maritime frontier, yet in battle captured not a single enemy, received but one wound, and was the first to shrink back, causing officers and soldiers to follow his example, rout the army, and abandon cities — the whole affair was child's play."

sentences.zh: 儻不置之法，不惟無以肅軍政而振人心，且何以慰死節諸臣於地下？

translations.literal: "If he were not punished by law, not only would military discipline and popular morale fail to be restored, but how could the officials who died for the state be comforted in the grave?"
translations.idiomatic: "If he were not punished, not only would military discipline and public morale fail to be restored, but how could the officials who died for the state be comforted beneath the earth?"

sentences.zh: 」步雲遂棄市。

translations.literal: Buyun was then executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Buyun was then executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：奕山、奕經，天潢貴冑，不諳軍旅，先後棄師，如出一轍，事乃益不可為。

translations.literal: [Commentary] The commentary says: Yishan and Yijing were noble scions of the imperial house, unacquainted with military affairs; they abandoned their armies in succession like the same pattern, and affairs became all the more impossible.
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The commentary says: Yishan and Yijing were noble scions of the imperial house, unacquainted with military affairs; they abandoned their armies in succession as if following the same pattern, and affairs became all the more impossible.

sentences.zh: 其人皆庸闇不足責，當時廷臣不能預計，疆吏不能匡救，可謂國無人焉。

translations.literal: The men themselves were all mediocre and dim and not worth blaming; at the time court ministers could not foresee events and frontier officials could not correct them — it may be said the state had no capable men.
translations.idiomatic: The men themselves were mediocre and not worth blaming; court ministers could not foresee events and frontier officials could not correct them — it may be said the state had no capable men.

sentences.zh: 奕山後復棄東北邊地，其貽患尤深。

translations.literal: Yishan afterward again abandoned the northeastern borderlands, and the harm he left was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Yishan later again surrendered the northeastern borderlands, and the harm he left was especially deep.

sentences.zh: 餘步雲庸懦巧猾，卒膺顯戮。

translations.literal: Yu Buyun was mediocre, cowardly, and crafty, and in the end suffered conspicuous execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Buyun was mediocre, cowardly, and crafty, and in the end suffered public execution.

sentences.zh: 宣宗於僨事諸人，皆從寬典，伸軍律者，僅步雲一人耳。

translations.literal: The Daoguang Emperor toward all those who failed in affairs used lenient treatment; only in extending military law to Buyun was there a single case.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoguang Emperor treated all who failed in these affairs with leniency; only in extending military law to Buyun was there a single exception.
